evidence: [inferred: grows in swamps or marshes] It is found in a variety of habitats, from deep sandy loams to gravelly or sandy sites on gentle slopes, and in the north-east of the range, on seasonally swampy ground.

Nicolle (2005) clarifies the habit of plants at the type locality of E. sargentii, Mears Lake, south of Quairading, stating that they are "non-lignotuberous, obligate-seeder" i.e. mallets, not mallees.
It survives well in sheltered situations in heavily frosted areas like Canberra.
